title: Brush teeth, read, then go to bed
subtitle: Repeat a familiar bedtime routine
description: Help your child brush their teeth, read together, and go to bed at a regular time.

title: Dim the bedroom lights before bed
subtitle: Use a dim night-light if needed
description: For ages 3–18, reduce bedroom light at bedtime; use a dim, warm-coloured night-light if needed.

title: Put screens away before bedtime
subtitle: Keep devices out of the bedroom
description: For ages 3–18, stop screens at least an hour before bed and keep devices outside the bedroom overnight.

title: Spend time in morning daylight
subtitle: Make room for natural light
description: For ages 3–18, encourage time in natural daylight, especially in the morning.

title: Keep bedtime and waking times regular
subtitle: Follow a similar schedule on weekends
description: For ages 3–18, keep bedtimes and wake-up times within 1–2 hours across the week.

title: Use the toilet before bed
subtitle: For children being supported with bedwetting
description: Encourage a toilet visit before bed and make the toilet easy to reach at night. This is situation-specific guidance, not a requirement for every child.

title: Make time for bedtime worries
subtitle: Listen and plan when to talk further
description: For ages 3–18, acknowledge bedtime worries; arrange a daytime conversation if they need more discussion.

title: Offer a variety of plant foods
subtitle: Include fruit, vegetables and whole grains
description: Offer fruit, vegetables and whole-grain foods across meals, rather than repeatedly relying on the same foods.

title: Let your child stop eating when full
subtitle: Offer food without pressure to finish
description: Provide meals and snacks at predictable times, and let your child decide whether they are hungry and when they have eaten enough.

title: Share a relaxed family meal
subtitle: Make room for friendly conversation
description: Eat together when possible and keep mealtime conversation pleasant, without arguments or lectures.

title: Offer different protein foods
subtitle: Vary the choices across meals
description: Include protein foods such as beans, eggs, fish or lean meat as part of varied meals.

title: Offer water instead of sugary drinks
subtitle: Make water an everyday option
description: Offer water in place of soda and other sugary drinks.

title: Eat without commenting on their body
subtitle: No “you look” or “you need to eat more”
description: During meals, skip comments about their body, weight, or how much they “should” eat. Done when the meal ended without those comments.

title: Offer new foods alongside familiar ones
subtitle: For toddlers learning to enjoy different foods
description: Serve a small amount of a new food with familiar foods. Offer it again on another occasion without bargaining over bites.

title: Walk or cycle together on short trips
subtitle: Build movement into family travel
description: When practical, walk or cycle together for short journeys instead of taking the car.

title: Spread active play throughout the day
subtitle: Under age 5: at least 180 minutes of daily activity
description: Ages 1–2: Offer movement and play across the day, such as walking, dancing and playing outdoors. The time can be spread out. Ages 3–4: Include at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity within the day’s movement, spread across the day.

title: Build an active week
subtitle: Ages 5–18: average 60 minutes of activity daily
description: Aim for an average of at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity per day across the week, using activities suited to your child’s abilities.

title: Practise throwing and catching through play
subtitle: For young children developing movement skills
description: Play throwing-and-catching games suited to your child’s age and ability.

title: Let them play freely outside
subtitle: You stay nearby. You do not run the game.
description: Give them unstructured outdoor play without directing the activity. Stay nearby for safety. Done when they played without your plan.

title: Break up long periods of sitting
subtitle: For school-age children and teenagers
description: Encourage your child to break up long periods of sitting with movement throughout the day.

title: Choose an active game your child enjoys
subtitle: For ages 5–18: running, cycling or dancing
description: Encourage enjoyable activity such as running games, cycling or dancing as part of their movement across the week.

title: Brush teeth morning and night
subtitle: Two minutes each time. You help as needed.
description: Brush morning and night for two minutes. For younger kids, you do most of it. For older kids, you check. Done when both brushes happened.

variants.2-4y: You brush their teeth morning and night for two minutes. They can hold the brush after. Done when both brushes happened.
variants.5-8y: They brush; you finish the two minutes morning and night. Done when both brushes happened.
variants.9-12y: They brush morning and night for two minutes. You check once. Done when both brushes happened.
variants.13-18y: They brush morning and night for two minutes. A reminder is enough. Done when both brushes happened.

title: Wash hands before eating and after the toilet
subtitle: Use soap, scrub, rinse and dry
description: Help your child wash with soap and water before eating and after using the toilet, scrubbing for at least 20 seconds.

title: Put on sunscreen before a long time outside
subtitle: Face, neck, and arms before you go
description: Put sunscreen on face, neck, and arms before extended outdoor time. Done when it is on before you leave.

title: Bring a water bottle to school
subtitle: Fill it the night before or at breakfast
description: Fill a water bottle and put it with the bag they take to school. Done when it is packed.

title: Change into clean clothes after heavy activity
subtitle: Sweaty clothes go in the hamper
description: After sports or heavy play, change into clean clothes and put the sweaty ones in the hamper. Done when they changed.

title: Build a personal hygiene routine
subtitle: For teenagers going through puberty
description: Help your teen establish washing, hair-care and toothbrushing routines, and discuss using deodorant kindly and privately.

title: Practise slow breathing together
subtitle: Learn the exercise when everyone is calm
description: In a quiet moment, practise breathing slowly in through the nose and out through the mouth. Start with one breath for younger children.

title: Notice the early signs of anger
subtitle: Look for changes in the body
description: Help your child recognise their own warning signs, such as tense muscles, clenched fists or a faster heartbeat.

title: Help your child name their feelings
subtitle: Connect the feeling to what happened
description: Listen to what happened and help your young child find words for the emotion they are experiencing.

title: Choose a strategy for when anger builds
subtitle: Practise a response your child can use
description: Help your child choose a response such as slow breathing, walking away or talking to someone they trust when they notice anger starting.

title: Talk about what to do differently next time
subtitle: For ages 3–8, after they have calmed down
description: Once your child is calm, discuss what happened and an alternative response, such as asking for a toy instead of hitting.

title: Notice progress in handling anger
subtitle: Recognise small efforts to cope
description: Praise your child’s attempts to manage anger, including small improvements in how they respond.

title: Stay close while big feelings settle
subtitle: For ages 3–8: offer calm support
description: Keep yourself and your child safe, acknowledge their feelings, and stay available. Discuss solutions after they are calmer.

title: Spend focused time together
subtitle: Let your child choose an activity and give them your attention.
description: Set aside one-to-one time to talk or play together. Follow your child’s lead, with your phone and television put away.

title: Listen with your full attention
subtitle: Get to your child’s level and check that you understood.
description: Give your child your attention, come down to their level when helpful, and listen without interrupting. Reflect back what you understood and let them clarify.

title: Ask what support they want
subtitle: Check before offering advice
description: Listen first, then ask whether your child wants you to listen or help them work through a solution.

title: Talk about school and friendships
subtitle: For ages 6–10: explore what went well or felt hard
description: Ask about friends, enjoyable experiences and difficulties, then listen to how your child feels about them.

title: Give one clear instruction at a time
subtitle: For ages 2–4: name the specific action
description: Get your child’s attention, give one simple direction, and make the action concrete, such as putting a truck away.

title: Give a 5-minute warning
subtitle: Name the next thing before you switch
description: Before play or a screen ends, say “Five more minutes, then bath.” Done when you gave the warning before the switch.

title: Let one natural consequence happen
subtitle: You do not rescue the forgotten item
description: Let one natural consequence stand, like a forgotten item staying forgotten. Stay kind. Done when you did not rescue it.

title: Teach an age-appropriate household task
subtitle: Practise together before expecting independence
description: Choose a chore suited to your child’s abilities, explain it, and do it together while they learn.

title: Let them try the small problem first
subtitle: Wait, then one hint if they are stuck
description: When a small problem shows up, let them try first. Count to 20, then offer one hint if they are stuck. Done when they tried before you took over.

title: Let them dress themselves
subtitle: You lay out options. They put them on.
description: Let them dress themselves. Lay out two options if they need help choosing. Done when they put the clothes on, even if they are mismatched.

title: Let them clean up their own spill
subtitle: Hand them a cloth. Help only if needed.
description: Hand them a cloth and let them clean the spill. Help only if they cannot finish. Done when they started the cleanup.

title: Let them ask the question
subtitle: At a store, restaurant, or school office
description: Let them order or ask the question themselves at a store, restaurant, or office. You stand nearby. Done when they asked.

title: Put dirty clothes in the hamper
subtitle: The clothes they took off today
description: Put today’s dirty clothes in the hamper. Done when they are in the basket, not on the floor.

title: Put toys away together
subtitle: Start with a manageable chore for young children
description: Help your young child put toys away, giving them support as they learn the task.

title: Let your child help measure ingredients while you cook
subtitle: Help them fill measuring cups and compare amounts.
description: During a suitable cooking activity, help your child fill and level measuring cups and compare quantities.

title: Agree who does each household job
subtitle: Make responsibilities clear
description: Discuss suitable chores together and use a list or chart to show who is responsible and when each job needs doing.

title: Child clears their own plate
subtitle: To the sink or the counter
description: They carry their plate to the sink or counter after the meal. Done when the plate is there.

title: Thank someone for helping
subtitle: Name the person and what they did
description: Thank someone in the house for a specific help. Done when the thank-you named the person and the action.

title: Compare prices and features with your teen before choosing a phone plan
subtitle: Discuss which option fits the family’s needs and budget.
description: When choosing a phone plan with your teen, compare features and costs together against the family’s needs and budget.

title: Invite your child to describe the pictures while you read together
subtitle: Build on their comments without turning reading into a quiz.
description: With a preschooler, invite comments about the pictures, build on their answers and follow their interest. Keep it enjoyable rather than questioning them on every page.

title: Explore the answer together when your child asks how something works
subtitle: Observe, look it up or try a simple experiment.
description: When your child wonders about something, explore the answer together through observation or a simple experiment. You do not need to know the answer beforehand.

title: Let your child draw or paint without copying a sample
subtitle: Provide materials and let them choose what to make.
description: For young children, provide blank paper and suitable drawing or craft materials. Let them explore without copying a model or having their work corrected.

title: Create a list together of things your child can do when bored
subtitle: Choose activities they enjoy; use pictures for younger children.
description: Create a list together based on your child’s interests. Use pictures for younger children, and let them refer to it during free time.

title: Meet as a family each week to discuss plans and concerns
subtitle: Give everyone a turn to speak and write down agreements.
description: For families with school-age children, meet at a regular weekly time, let everyone speak without interruption, and record agreements. Keep reprimands out of the meeting.

title: Help your child draw or photograph something they noticed in nature
subtitle: Record what interested them so you can revisit it together.
description: When something interests your child—a plant, the moon or changing leaves—help them record their observations so they can revisit them.

title: Check upcoming work and deadlines
subtitle: Help school-age children plan ahead
description: Use a calendar or planner to keep track of assignments and due dates, and decide when the work will happen.

title: Set up a quiet homework space
subtitle: Keep supplies ready and distractions away
description: Provide a well-lit workspace with needed materials, and reduce distractions such as television and phone calls.

title: Divide a large assignment into smaller parts
subtitle: Plan manageable work sessions
description: Help your child break a big assignment into sections and make a schedule for completing them.

title: Give one genuine compliment
subtitle: About something specific they noticed
description: Give one specific compliment about something they actually noticed. Done when the sentence was said.

title: Help your child invite a friend over to play
subtitle: Let them choose whom to invite and coordinate with the other parent.
description: Ask your school-age child whom they would like to invite, then coordinate with the other parent. Give the children space to play while remaining available.

title: Play a card or board game to teach your child to take turns
subtitle: Explain each turn and help when waiting is difficult.
description: Play a suitable card or board game and explain whose turn comes next. Offer support while your child learns, instead of requiring independent turn-taking immediately.

title: Respect a child’s right to say no to touch
subtitle: Their body belongs to them
description: Teach your child that they can refuse unwanted touch, including from someone they know, and respect their refusal.

title: Practise how your child can leave bullying and get adult help
subtitle: Discuss speaking up when safe, walking away and telling a trusted adult.
description: Discuss what your child can do if bullied: speak firmly if safe, move away when it is not, and seek help from a trusted adult.

title: Help your child repair the harm if they have bullied someone
subtitle: Choose a response linked to the harm, such as repairing damaged belongings.
description: Only when your child has bullied someone: involve them in an appropriate repair, such as fixing damaged property or writing an apology. Do not force a meeting with the child who was harmed.

title: Ask before touching or borrowing
subtitle: Wait for a yes
description: Ask before hugging, grabbing, or borrowing. Wait for a yes. Done when they asked first.

title: Practice disagreeing without insults
subtitle: “I see it differently” counts
description: Practice disagreeing without insults. “I see it differently” counts. Done when a disagreement stayed respectful.

title: Tell a trusted adult about worrying touch or secrets
subtitle: Help your child know where to seek support
description: Explain that they can tell a trusted adult about anything that worries or upsets them, even if someone asked them to keep it secret.

title: Volunteer with your child in an activity suitable for their age
subtitle: Choose a community activity where you can help together.
description: Include your child in a suitable community activity, such as helping with a food-bank meal. Choose an opportunity that welcomes children and fits their abilities.

title: Get to know your teen’s friends
subtitle: Make their friends welcome at home
description: Create opportunities to meet the friends your teen spends time with, including welcoming them into your home.

title: Talk with your teen about caring behaviour and controlling behaviour in relationships
subtitle: Discuss personal choices, friendships, pressure and respectful disagreement.
description: With your teen, discuss being able to keep friendships, make choices and disagree safely. Explain how controlling behaviour differs from care.

title: Praise a specific effort or action
subtitle: Describe what your child did and why you appreciated it.
description: Recognise your child’s effort or helpful behaviour by naming the action you noticed, rather than giving a general label about what kind of person they are.

title: Let your child do their own homework
subtitle: Offer guidance without taking over
description: Be available to explain or suggest an approach, while letting your child do the thinking and complete the work themselves.

title: Ask “What did you learn?” after something hard
subtitle: After a miss, not only after a win
description: After something hard, ask what they learned. Done when they answered and you did not jump to a lecture.

title: Ask your child to show you the apps and games they use
subtitle: Learn what they do there and how they interact with other people.
description: Let your child walk you through a platform they use so you understand its features and how they interact with others there.

title: Agree on screen-use limits together
subtitle: Include screen-free times in your family media plan.
description: Create a family media plan with expectations and limits suited to your child. Agree on screen-free times such as meals, homework and bedtime, and have adults follow the plan too.

title: Point out advertisements while watching online content with your child
subtitle: Explain when a video or influencer is promoting something.
description: When viewing content together, help your child distinguish advertising, edited material and an influencer’s promotional message.

title: Use the correct names for body parts
subtitle: Use accurate words when body questions come up.
description: Use correct anatomical terms calmly when discussing the body or answering your child’s questions.

title: Agree on a check-in plan before going out
subtitle: For ages 9–18: discuss whereabouts and contact
description: Agree where your child is going, who they will be with, and when and how they will check in.

title: Seatbelt check before driving
subtitle: Click, then the car moves
description: Check that every seatbelt is on before the car moves. Done when you checked and then drove.

title: Helmet on before bike or scooter
subtitle: Strapped, then they roll
description: Put a helmet on before a bike, scooter, or skateboard. Done when it is strapped before they roll.

title: Set up privacy and messaging controls before your child uses a new account
subtitle: Review who can contact them, reporting tools and purchase permissions.
description: When an age-appropriate account is created, use secure privacy settings and discuss who can contact them, reporting tools and purchase permissions. Explain why passwords should not be shared with friends.

title: Ask permission before sharing someone’s photo
subtitle: Respect a no or a change of mind
description: Ask the people pictured before sharing their photo or video. Remove it if they later ask you to.

title: Tell an adult about a disturbing message
subtitle: They are not in trouble for showing you
description: Tell them they can show you a disturbing message and will not be in trouble. Done when you said that out loud.

title: Talk about consent and boundaries
subtitle: One short, judgment-free conversation
description: Have one short talk about consent and boundaries without judgment. Done when you talked and they could respond.

title: Agree how your teen can contact you to leave a situation involving alcohol or drugs
subtitle: Practise refusing an offer and choose a message or code word for help.
description: With your teen, practise declining an offer and agree on an exit plan, such as a code word they can text a family member.

title: Answer one body question honestly
subtitle: Short, true, and without teasing
description: Answer one body question honestly and without teasing. Done when you answered in plain words.

title: Normalize one puberty change
subtitle: Name it as expected, not weird
description: Name one puberty change as expected. Done when you said it in a matter-of-fact way.

title: Keep personal-care supplies available
subtitle: Make needed products easy to access
description: Ensure your teen has the washing, deodorant, skin-care or menstrual products they need.

title: Prepare for periods together
subtitle: Explain what to expect and pack supplies
description: Talk about periods before they begin, and help your child keep spare menstrual products and underwear somewhere accessible.

title: Let them ask an awkward question without teasing
subtitle: Thank them for asking
description: When an awkward question comes, thank them for asking and skip the tease. Done when the question got a straight answer.

title: Talk about body changes without commenting on looks
subtitle: No “you look grown” or rating
description: Talk about body changes without commenting on attractiveness. Done when the talk stayed about function, not looks.

title: Remind them bodies develop at different speeds
subtitle: Early and late are both normal
description: Remind them that bodies develop at different speeds. Done when you said early and late are both normal.

title: Say clearly what you want your child to do
subtitle: For ages 2–4: use a calm, specific direction
description: Describe the action you want in a calm voice instead of only telling your child what to stop doing.

title: Explain consequences calmly and follow through
subtitle: Give a clear opportunity to change behaviour
description: Explain a realistic consequence, allow your child a chance to respond, and follow through calmly and consistently if needed.

title: Apologise to your child after shouting or treating them unfairly
subtitle: Own your behaviour and explain what you will do differently.
description: When you make a parenting mistake, acknowledge it, apologise without shifting blame, and explain how you intend to do better.

title: Express love without tying it to achievement
subtitle: For ages 6–10: offer reassurance and affection
description: Let your child know they are loved through words and affection, including when they have made a mistake.

title: Respect your teen’s everyday privacy
subtitle: Knock and ask before entering personal space
description: Knock before entering their room, ask before looking in their bag, and discuss privacy boundaries together.

title: Offer two acceptable choices
subtitle: For ages 2–4: give a manageable decision
description: Offer two options that both work for the situation, allowing your child to make the choice.

title: Agree on household rules with your teen
subtitle: Discuss expectations and consequences together
description: Involve your teenager in setting family rules and the consequences of breaking them.

title: Use “When → Then”
subtitle: “When your shoes are on, then we leave.”
description: Use one When-Then: “When your shoes are on, then we leave.” Done when you used that frame once.

title: Keep the consequence related to the behavior
subtitle: The fix matches what happened
description: Pick a consequence that matches the behavior, not a random punishment. Done when the follow-through was related.

title: Pause before responding when you are angry
subtitle: Give yourself a moment to regain calm
description: Take a pause and several slow breaths before responding to your child when your own anger is rising.

title: Give one respectful redo
subtitle: “Try saying that again respectfully.”
description: Offer one redo: “Try saying that again respectfully.” Done when you offered the redo and heard a second try.

title: Gather what is needed before starting a task
subtitle: Help school-age children prepare to work
description: Identify the task and collect the materials needed before beginning.

title: Use a checklist for a multi-step task
subtitle: Make the steps of a routine visible.
description: Help your child list the steps of a task or routine, such as getting ready in the morning, and mark them off as they finish.

title: Plan breaks during longer homework sessions
subtitle: Balance focused work with rest
description: Help your child schedule breaks when homework needs a longer work session.

title: Use a visual timer to show your child how much task time remains
subtitle: Offer this support when they struggle to judge passing time.
description: For a child who struggles with time management, use a visual timer or countdown clock during a task so they can see how much time remains.

title: Put finished homework in the school bag
subtitle: Complete the final step before moving on
description: After checking the work is complete, place it in the appropriate folder and school bag.

title: Ask an open question about a worry
subtitle: Give your child room to explain
description: Ask how they feel about a situation without suggesting that they should be afraid of it.

title: Talk through a plan for a feared situation
subtitle: Work out what they could do
description: Discuss what your child could do if the situation they worry about happened, rather than promising it cannot happen.

title: Do one small brave step
subtitle: To the door is enough. Not the whole thing.
description: Pick one small brave step, like walking to the classroom door. Done when they did that step.

title: Offer reassurance without promising certainty
subtitle: Show confidence in their ability to cope
description: Acknowledge that a situation feels difficult and express confidence that your child can manage it with support.

title: Use a short, predictable goodbye
subtitle: For young children adjusting to separation
description: Use a familiar goodbye ritual, give your child your attention, and explain when you will return using an event they understand.

title: Recognise effort in facing a worry
subtitle: Notice the attempt, not just the outcome
description: Praise your child for tolerating an anxious situation and making an effort to face it.

title: Help siblings work towards an agreement
subtitle: For teenagers: listen to both perspectives
description: When help is needed, let each teen explain their view, support a calm discussion and help them negotiate a solution.

title: Don’t compare siblings
subtitle: No “Why can’t you be more like…”
description: Skip any comparison to a sibling today. Done when the day ended without one.

title: Notice teamwork between siblings
subtitle: Name the moment they helped each other
description: Name one moment they helped each other. Done when they heard the sentence.

title: Let them own one morning step
subtitle: Teeth, clothes, bag, or breakfast setup
description: Pick one part of the morning they do without you taking over: teeth, clothes, bag, or breakfast setup. Done when they finished that step.

title: Choose a regular homework time that fits your child
subtitle: Allow for a snack or play beforehand if helpful
description: Agree on a study time that suits your child; some work better after a snack and play, while others prefer later.

title: Finish one small responsibility before leisure
subtitle: Bag, clothes, pet, or dishes — then free time
description: Ask for one small responsibility before leisure: bag away, clothes away, pet, or dishes. Done when that job finished first.

title: Ask your child what they want you to discuss at their teacher meeting
subtitle: Take their questions and concerns into the conversation.
description: Before a primary-school teacher meeting, ask what your child wants discussed. Take those questions along and ask how you can support learning at home.

title: Help your child choose something to save for and plan how to afford it
subtitle: For ages 6–9, connect saving with a specific goal.
description: For ages 6–9, help your child identify a specific savings goal and make a plan to reach it.
